MUQATIL:10:47-49/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:10:47-49/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:10:47-49/r4.claim: Every nation has an appointed time because mercy preceded wrath; punishment arrives exactly on time, neither delayed nor advanced.

TAB-FULL:v12p189#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p189#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p189#3/r1.claim: Muhammad is told to answer those demanding the promised punishment: he controls neither harm nor benefit for himself in worldly or religious matters except by God's will, and is even less able to know the unseen or Hour without permission.

TAB-FULL:v12p189#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p189#3/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p189#3/r2.claim: Every community has a fixed term for its life; when it arrives, none can delay or advance it because God decreed its time.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1955#4/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1955#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1955#4/r1.claim: Mujahid says the Prophet cannot control his own benefit or harm, including guidance, except as God wills.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1955#4/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1955#4/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1955#4/r2.claim: Hasan rebukes people for asking God to prolong someone's life when every community has an appointed term that cannot be delayed or advanced.

SULAMI:v1p303#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p303#3/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p303#3/r1.claim: The most particular servant owns nothing independently and cannot control even personal harm or benefit; recognizing that all belongs to God frees one from seeking people's praise.

THALABI:v5p134/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p134/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p134/r11.claim: The Prophet controls neither harm nor benefit for himself except by God’s will; each community has a fixed lifespan, neither delayed nor advanced by an hour.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p220/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p220/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p220/r1.claim: The explanation of this verse is given under 7:34 and 7:188.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:48-49/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:48-49/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:10:48-49/r2.claim: The statement that Muhammad controls neither harm nor benefit except by God's will, and that each nation has a fixed term, is explained in two verses of al-Aʿrāf.

JISHUMI:v5p3376#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3376#2/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3376#2/r2.claim: An ajal is the fixed, latent time at which an event occurs; bayāt is the arrival of something at night, and istijāl seeks something before its proper time.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p136#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p136#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p136#2/r5.claim: The Prophet cannot independently bring harm or benefit to himself, except what God wills him to control.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p136#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p136#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p136#2/r6.claim: Each nation has a set lifetime; when it ends, its people can neither delay nor advance it.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p333#4/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p333#4/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p333#4/r2.claim: The Prophet cannot independently bring himself harm such as illness or poverty, or benefit such as health or wealth; the exception is disconnected, meaning whatever God wills happens.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p333#4/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p333#4/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p333#4/r3.claim: Each nation has a fixed term for punishment, fulfilled without fail, so they should not demand it early.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p333#4/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p333#4/r4.speaker: ابن سيرين
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p333#4/r4.claim: Ibn Sirin read فإذا جاء آجالهم with the plural ‘terms.’

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p123#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p123#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p123#2/r5.claim: Muhammad is told to say he controls neither harm nor benefit for himself apart from God's will and remains under God's power and need of His grace; therefore he cannot claim knowledge of the unseen or defy God's command.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p123#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p123#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p123#2/r6.claim: Each nation's term is known only to God; when death or destruction comes, it cannot be delayed or brought forward by even an hour.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p123#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p123#2/r7.speaker: ابن سيرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p123#2/r7.claim: Ibn Sirin reads آجالهم in the plural.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p38/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p38/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p38/r1.claim: The interpretation of this verse was given in the discussions of 7:34 and 7:188.

RAZI-FULL:v17p86#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p86#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p86#2/r1.claim: The question about when the threat will arrive is the fifth objection to prophecy: disbelievers take its delay as evidence against the Prophet.

RAZI-FULL:v17p86#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p86#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p86#2/r3.claim: The Prophet's answer is that only God controls harm, benefit, punishment, and rescue; God had not fixed a time for the threat, whether timing follows unconstrained will or a wise benefit.

RAZI-FULL:v17p86#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p86#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p86#2/r4.claim: Once God's appointed time arrives, the event must occur then and cannot be advanced or delayed.

RAZI-FULL:v17p87/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p87/r1.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v17p87/r1.claim: The Muʿtazilites invoke the exception in the Prophet's lack of independent power to argue that human control over harm and benefit depends on God's will.

RAZI-FULL:v17p87/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p87/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p87/r2.claim: The appointed-term wording means no one dies before their term ends; even a person killed is killed only at that appointed time, a debate treated elsewhere in the work.

RAZI-FULL:v17p87/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p87/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v17p87/r3.claim: Grammatically the conditional's فاء introduces its result, showing that the result occurs with the condition rather than later; the particle marks consequence, not delay.

RAZI-FULL:v17p87/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p87/r4.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v17p87/r4.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī rules invalid a husband's conditional divorce of a woman he has not yet married; Rāzī argues the result would have to coincide with the marriage and unite opposites.

RAZI-FULL:v17p87/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v17p87/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v17p87/r5.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa rules that such a conditional divorce is valid, a position Rāzī rejects using the verse's account of a result coinciding with its condition.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:49/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:49/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:49/r1.claim: When people demanded punishment, the Prophet was told he controls neither harm nor benefit for himself except as God wills, so he cannot control their punishment either.

QURTUBI-FULL:10:49/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:10:49/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:10:49/r2.claim: Every nation has a time fixed in God’s knowledge for destruction and punishment; when it arrives, no one can delay or advance it even by an hour.

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:49-50/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:49-50/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:49-50/r1.claim: The Prophet's inability to harm or benefit himself means he cannot bring punishment upon his people at will; only what God wills is within his power or comes to pass.

BAYDAWI-FULL:10:49-50/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:49-50/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:10:49-50/r2.claim: Every nation has an appointed time for destruction; it cannot move that time forward or back, so the threatened moment will arrive without need to hasten it.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p131#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p131#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p131#4/r1.claim: Muhammad cannot control harm such as illness or poverty, nor benefit such as health or wealth, except what God wills; the exception is disconnected: what God wills nevertheless occurs.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p131#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p131#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p131#4/r2.claim: Therefore he cannot bring the audience harm or punishment by his own power.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p131#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p131#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p131#4/r3.claim: Every nation has a fixed, written time for punishment and cannot advance or delay it; the warning is not to demand haste.

QASHANI:10:48-49/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:10:48-49/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:10:48-49/r2.claim: Saying he controls neither harm nor benefit guides them toward witnessing divine acts by denying independent ownership and efficacy to the self.

QASHANI:10:48-49/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:10:48-49/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:10:48-49/r3.claim: The lesser resurrection occurs when each community reaches its appointed term.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p67/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p67/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p67/r4.claim: Since the Prophet cannot independently bring harm or benefit even to himself, he cannot control their punishment or know its timing without God's disclosure; God alone knows each community's appointed term.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p67/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p67/r5.speaker: ابن سيرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p67/r5.claim: Ibn Sīrīn reads آجالهم in the plural.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p67/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p67/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p67/r6.claim: The exception ما شاء الله can be connected: except what God wills him to control; the appointed term is a fixed time for their punishment.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p67/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p67/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p67/r7.claim: Zamakhshari treats the exception as disconnected: rather, whatever God wills will occur, so the Prophet cannot bring harm or punishment himself.

SAMIN-DURR:10:49/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:49/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:10:49/r1.claim: إلا ما شاء الله may be a connected exception: what God wills me to possess or control is excluded.

SAMIN-DURR:10:49/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:10:49/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:10:49/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads it as disconnected: whatever God wills will occur, so the speaker cannot control harm or bring punishment.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p273/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p273/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p273/r1.claim: Disbelievers' demand to know when punishment will come is useless; believers know the Hour is certain even if its exact time is unknown.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p273/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p273/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p273/r2.claim: The Messenger controls neither harm nor benefit except by God's will, speaks only what God teaches, and was told the Hour would occur but not when.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p273/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p273/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p273/r3.claim: Every community has a measured term; when it arrives, no delay or advancement is possible.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p449/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p449/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p449/r6.claim: Muhammad has no independent control of harm or benefit, even for himself; all capacity is subject to God's will, and every community has an appointed term that cannot be advanced or delayed.

BIQAI-FULL:v3p449/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p449/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p449/r7.claim: Because the context concerns vengeance, harm comes first; blessings are more numerous, so people should be grateful rather than wish for harm, and the author explains the forms of the words for delay and advance.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p130/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p130/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p130/r1.claim: The Prophet cannot control harm or benefit; harm comes first because the passage stresses inability to bring punishment, while benefit completes the expression of total helplessness.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p130/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p130/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p130/r2.claim: A second explanation calls mention of benefit a digression to prevent readers from thinking incapacity applies only to harm; the order is reversed in al-Aʿrāf because benefit is then central.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p130/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p130/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p130/r3.claim: The disconnected-exception reading means that whatever God wills will occur; the connected reading means whatever He wills the Prophet to control.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p130/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p130/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p130/r4.claim: The Muʿtazilites use a connected exception to argue that people independently control their acts, but al-Ālūsī says the verse falls far short of proving this.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p130/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p130/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p130/r5.claim: Some proponents of the Salaf's view infer that human capacity has an effect only by God's permission, between the Jabriyya denial of capacity, the common Ashʿarī denial of its efficacy, and the Muʿtazilī claim of independent effect.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p130/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p130/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p130/r6.claim: If ملك means ability, the exception is connected; if it retains literal ownership, it must be disconnected, though connection is the default whenever it works without strain.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p131#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131#2/r1.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭībī says the reply uses a wise redirection: the questioners mockingly demand a time, but the Prophet disavows control over even his own affairs before answering properly.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p131#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131#2/r2.claim: The substantive answer is that God has fixed a time for the promised punishment, which will inevitably be fulfilled, so the people should not hasten it.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p131#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131#2/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī explains omission of fa before the deadline condition as presenting it as independently established, while the fa in the consequence strengthens the condition's necessary result.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p131#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131#2/r4.claim: The relation to the preceding clause may clarify the exception and qualify the decree; this is a possible account of the sentence connection.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p131#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131#2/r5.speaker: صفاء الدين عيسى البندنيجي
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131#2/r5.claim: Al-Bandhanījī says the passage consoles the Prophet against mockery: each clause stands independently for emphasis, unlike al-Aʿrāf, which directly threatens Meccans and links the warning with fa.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p131#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131#2/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī ridicules a grammarian's claim that the differing connective particles merely show two forms are both grammatically possible; the Quran's purpose is eloquence, not grammar instruction.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p131/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131/r1.claim: The second clause may prohibit both delay and advance; placing impossible advance beside delay intensifies the impossibility, and istifʿāl can suggest that even seeking it is inconceivable.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p131/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats denial of advancing or delaying as an idiom for a fixed, appointed limit, illustrated by a line from al-Ḥamāsa.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p131/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131/r3.speaker: المرزوقي
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131/r3.claim: Al-Marzūqī explains the cited poem as the lover remaining with his beloved in every situation, whether she stays or departs.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p131/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131/r4.claim: The verse is an independent part of the answer, and the order of denying delay before advance has already been discussed under al-Aʿrāf.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p131/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131/r5.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the claim that the exception shifts the subject from the Prophet to God, as though only God owns and does whatever He wills.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p131/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131/r6.claim: Each community has a fixed time appointed for its punishment, which does not transfer to another community.

ALUSI-FULL:v11p131/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v11p131/r7.claim: The wording specifies each community's own deadline; أجل can mean its fixed time limit, whose arrival means its completion, and ساعة denotes a tiny interval.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p188#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p188#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p188#2/r1.claim: The verse follows 10:46: whether punishment is hastened or delayed is equal to God because the full punishment is in the afterlife; it then answers their taunting about delay.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p188#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p188#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p188#2/r2.claim: The imperfect صيغة presents their repeated taunt; الوعد means the promised punishment, and asking when it comes means when it will appear.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p188#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p188#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p188#2/r3.claim: Their question signals impatience and indifference, then indirectly reveals disbelief: demanding a time means they do not expect the threat to arrive.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p188#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p188#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p188#2/r4.claim: The threatened event here is punishment in worldly life.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p188#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p188#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p188#2/r5.claim: The plural challenge addresses the Prophet mockingly, as in 15:6 and 25:7; Abu Bakr al-Aswad's verse likewise mocks the claim of resurrection.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p188#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p188#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p188#2/r6.claim: The address may include the Prophet and believers to sow doubt, but only the Prophet is told to answer because he conveyed the warning and believers follow him.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r1.claim: The Prophet's denial of ownership means he cannot effect harm or benefit by his own power.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r2.claim: Harm comes first because the audience awaited a threat; harm is easier to cause, so benefit after it is a rhetorical ascent.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r3.claim: Mentioning both harm and benefit comprehensively covers the two kinds of conditions.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r4.claim: The exception is disconnected and means “but”: whatever benefits or harms me is only what God wills.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r5.claim: The answer refutes their challenge by a demonstrative argument: if he cannot control even his own welfare, he cannot bring their promised punishment.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r6.claim: A person's nearest possible control would concern the self, yet benefits and harms depend on interlinked events beyond human control, so people are directed by God's power.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r7.claim: The promised punishment comes from God, not the Prophet, and has a divinely fixed time.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p189/r8.claim: “Every community has a term” explains why he cannot set the punishment: God appoints each community's term wisely, including its punishment.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p190/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p190/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p190/r1.claim: The universal premise includes the addressees: they are a community, so they too have a term and should await it.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p190/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p190/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p190/r2.claim: The clause beginning “when their term comes” describes the term as fixed and unchangeable.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p190/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p190/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v11p190/r3.claim: “When” carries conditional force, so the following fa marks its clause as the consequence.

TABATABAI:10:48-49/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:48-49/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:48-49/r4.claim: The Prophet cannot bring himself harm or benefit except by God’s will; all command belongs to God, so demanding that he hasten judgment is ignorant.

TABATABAI:10:48-49/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:48-49/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:48-49/r5.claim: The specific time is unseen and known only to God, as the surah has already stated.

TABATABAI:10:49/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:49/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:49/r1.claim: Every community has a fixed lifespan: once its term arrives it can neither be delayed nor advanced, and this law also applies to the Prophet’s people.

TABATABAI:10:49/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:49/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:49/r2.claim: Communities have a collective life beyond individual lifetimes, with their own lifespan, fortune, suffering, duties, guidance, error, reward, and punishment under divine governance.

TABATABAI:10:49/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:49/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:49/r3.claim: Ruined settlements and Qur’anic histories of Noah, ʿAd, Thamud, Abraham’s people, Lot’s cities, and Pharaoh’s Copts show that earlier peoples perished only after messengers brought proofs and most people rejected them.

TABATABAI:10:49/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:49/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:49/r4.claim: Because this community too divided over the truth, God will judge it as He judged earlier peoples; the warning reaches wrongdoers among the faithful as well as polytheists.

TABATABAI:10:49/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:10:49/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:10:49/r5.claim: He rejects the belief that this community is immune from worldly punishment because it is mercied for the Prophet’s sake; honor with God comes only through piety.

ASAD-NOTES:10:49#n69/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:10:49#n69/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:10:49#n69/r1.claim: The Prophet cannot predict matters beyond human perception because he has no supernatural powers.

ASAD-NOTES:10:49#n70/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:10:49#n70/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:10:49#n70/r1.claim: The fixed term refers especially to the Last Hour and the Day of Judgment.

ASAD-NOTES:10:49#n71/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:10:49#n71/r1.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:10:49#n71/r1.claim: Zamakhshari says all divine chastisement is so awful that sinners should wish to flee it; nothing in it should make them wish to hasten it.

ASAD-NOTES:10:49#n71/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:10:49#n71/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:10:49#n71/r2.claim: The question alludes to deniers' disbelief in the Hour and sarcastic demand for immediate punishment as proof of Muhammad's mission; doom comes suddenly.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: On the Day of Judgment, each soul would ransom itself with all worldly treasure if possible, showing why deniers should not call for doom.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The promised punishment may arrive during the Prophet’s life or later, but a messenger’s nation is certainly judged in this world.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Prophet's first response to the mock demand makes clear that he has no control over when punishment arrives; the timing belongs to God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: A nation's deadline is measured by moral standards: God grants respite until rebellion reaches the point fixed for destruction, and only He knows the duration.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:48/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:48/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:48/r1.claim: When the Prophet warned pagans about the afterlife, they mocked him, demanded to know when it would happen, and challenged him to bring it if he was truthful.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:48/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:48/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:10:48/r2.claim: God alone requites people for their deeds; nobody, including prophets, has this power, and no one can shorten or extend the divinely granted term of trial.

STUDYQURAN:10:49/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:10:49/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:10:49/r1.claim: In answer to Makkan idolaters demanding hastened punishment, the Prophet has no independent power to bring punishment or benefit; all depends on God’s will.

STUDYQURAN:10:49/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:10:49/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:10:49/r2.claim: Each community has a lifespan known only to God and perishes at its end, though it may be punished before its earthly term expires.
